about: Every claim the Rerankers lesson shows, with the mark the research note gives it: verified (note label V: primary text, card or code read), unverified (U), inferred (I: the note's own reading), ours (our run or our decision record). Source keys resolve in lesson-sources.json. The page shows each mark next to the claim.

claims.text: A cross-encoder reads the question and one passage together and outputs one relevance score; a bi-encoder embeds each text alone and compares vectors.
Why the cross-encoder is more accurate: in a bi-encoder the question and passage never see each other; in a cross-encoder every question word can attend to every passage word.
bge-reranker-v2-m3 outputs a raw logit and maps it to [0, 1] with a sigmoid; our educator_core/models.py does the same.
Reranking BM25 results with BERT on MS MARCO was the top leaderboard entry, 27% (relative) above the previous state of the art in MRR@10.
MRR@10 rose from 16.7 to 36.5 (detail recorded in the Indexing for RAG lesson; not re-read for the research note).
On BEIR, re-ranking and late-interaction models achieve the best zero-shot performance on average, at high computational cost.
On Q3 (a paraphrase), every first-stage list missed the answer chunk; only the reranker placed it 2nd. Three questions: a demo, not a test.
In the Qwen3-Reranker card's run (top 100 from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B), English MTEB-R: first stage alone 61.82, after bge-reranker-v2-m3 57.03; Chinese CMTEB-R 71.02 to 72.16.
So adding a reranker is not always a gain; it must be measured on our questions.
Measured rate: about 0.5 pairs/s on a Kaggle 4-CPU kernel, int8 ONNX, one pair at a time (run rerank-0: 1,477 pairs in 2,841 s).
In the product the graph arm scored 627 passages in 7-8 min before the cap of 60.
Memory about 0.9 GB; RERANKER_ENABLED=false saves it. The backend with encoder and reranker uses 2.05 GB.
Our Reranker truncates the pair to 512 tokens; the vendor evaluation used 1,024.
Long passages lose their tail at 512 tokens.
int8 ONNX results can depend on the CPU instruction set; this is why the thesis pins the scoring job.
claims.loc: ONNX Runtime docs, cited in Addendum D

claims.text: Model: BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3, 567.8M parameters, Apache-2.0, multilingual, built on bge-m3, released 2024-03-15.
The backend runs onnx/model_int8.onnx from onnx-community/bge-reranker-v2-m3-ONNX, an automatic ONNX conversion of the BAAI model, one pair at a time, lazy-loaded.

R list: BM25 + dense, RRF (k = 60); the cross-encoder scores the first rerank_top = 10 candidates (dev-tuned, C4), sorts them by score then id, and puts them before the rest; rerank_top 0 = no reranker anywhere.

Graph list: passages from the concept walk carry a hop number; rank rule 7 (the earlier rule) is hop ascending, then cross-encoder score descending, then id. Addendum D's hop-balanced/1 rule needs the score for every hop group and refuses to run without the reranker.
Product-only cap graph_ce_top_n = 60: above 60 passages in a hop group, only the 60 closest by dense score are scored. Thesis arms: no cap.

G1 abstention gate: s_max_rerank = highest reranker score among the packed passages; below tutor_tau_rerank = 0.05 the tutor abstains. Without the reranker it uses the best dense cosine (0.45). The thresholds are placeholders, not calibrated.
Older chat path: recall 20 candidates, rerank, keep top 5; a reranker failure falls back to the recall order. The HTTP engine was removed.
Thesis arm R = BM25 + pgvector BGE-M3, RRF k = 60, cross-encoder rerank, tuned on dev.
Stage A scores were to come from the same int8 ONNX file on Kaggle CPU (option S1), with an fp32 GPU re-score as the pre-committed fallback (S2).
BEIR: 18 English retrieval datasets in different domains, used zero-shot; metric nDCG@10.
MTEB v1: 8 embedding tasks, 58 datasets, 112 languages; reranking is one task type.
MIRACL: ad hoc retrieval in 18 languages over Wikipedia, 77K queries, 700K+ native-speaker judgements; includes Persian.

Card numbers (reranking the first stage's top 100): BEIR average 54.31 to 55.36 (bge-large-en-v1.5); MIRACL average 67.91 to 72.84 (bge-m3); MIRACL Persian 57.7 to 62.49; MIRACL English 59.6 to 63.45. Vendor numbers.
The metric on the card images is not printed; nDCG@10 is likely.
The BGE M3 paper describes the embedding model, not this reranker: its Table 1 has no bge-reranker-v2-m3 row. The reranker's numbers come only from the model card.
For scale: on MIRACL Persian (dev, nDCG@10) the BGE M3 paper gives BM25 28.7 and M3-Dense 60.9.
A reranker score depends on the first stage and the truncation length; two cards with different first stages cannot be compared row by row.
Qwen3-Reranker card run: bge-reranker-v2-m3 MTEB-R / CMTEB-R / MMTEB-R / MLDR = 57.03 / 72.16 / 58.36 / 59.51; Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B = 65.80 / 71.31 / 66.36 / 67.28.
jina-reranker-v2 card run: bge-reranker-v2-m3 MKQA / BEIR / MLDR = 54.17 / 53.65 / 59.73; jina-reranker-v2 (278M) = 54.83 / 53.17 / 68.95.
jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual: 278M, CC BY-NC 4.0 (research and evaluation; commercial via API), 1,024-token context.
mxbai-rerank-base-v2 / large-v2: 0.5B / 1.5B, Apache-2.0, BEIR 55.57 / 57.49 (card).
Qwen3-Reranker 0.6B / 4B / 8B, Apache-2.0: MMTEB-R 66.36 / 72.74 / 72.94; an LLM reranker (yes/no token), so its CPU int8 cost must be measured.

claims.text: Cohere Rerank is a commercial API with a per-search fee; it breaks the own-compute rule.

Recorded reasons for the choice: inherited and already wired (RERANK_ENGINE=local); the partner's HTTP reranker was unreachable and removed under 'own APIs only'; the Cohere fee would be the largest cost line ($15) of the offline evaluation; kept optional until it passed a Mac latency and memory gate; same family as our bge-m3 encoder.
Chosen because it is multilingual and covers Persian: true as a property, not found as a stated reason.
Chosen because of its size and an int8 CPU export: not found as a stated reason.
Compared against jina, mxbai or Qwen3 rerankers before the choice: no comparison found (probably not done).
A benchmark drove the choice: no record names BEIR or MIRACL as the reason.
It is a defensible default but no longer the strongest at its size; for the thesis this matters little because R and H share the same reranker.
Recommendation: keep it frozen for the thesis; one product test of Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B on our dev questions; calibrate the G1 gate; a small Persian check before Persian content goes live.
The Kaggle run of the Indexing lesson (FlagEmbedding, CPU) scored every chunk against each of the three questions.
A reranker can only promote a passage that the fast search already found; its job is order, not search.

S1 was kept: all 24 shards and the probe ran on Kaggle CPUs (Intel Xeon and AMD EPYC), and every kernel (25/25) was bit-equal on the 200-key overlap check, so the switch record says S1 and the S2 fallback did not run. The merged file holds 197,073 scores.

For H and Hc the thesis replaces rule 7's ordering with hop-balanced/1: the slots are shared across hops 0, 1 and 2 by a quota (4 / 3 / 3 at 10 slots), each hop takes its best passages by cross-encoder score, free slots are backfilled in rule-7 order, and the chosen list is output in rule-7 order (hop, descending score, id). Rule 7 stays only in an exploratory variant.
